original_question: For a br-graph H, let S_H be its switching graph. A 3-NU polymorphism phi : H^3 -> H satisfies phi(x, x, y) = phi(x, y, x) = phi(y, x, x) = x, and a polymorphism of S_H is called semi-conservative when it preserves symmetric lists. Is it true that S_H has a semi-conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism if and only if it has a semi-conservative 3-NU polymorphism?
target_in_paper: Proposition 1.2 in Section 1, i.e. the sharper introductory reformulation of Conjecture 1.1 that asks whether the semi-conservative weak near-unanimity condition on the switching graph can be replaced by a semi-conservative ternary near-unanimity condition; Theorem 1.3 then confirms the refined characterisation for reflexive br-graphs. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.07764))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s br-graph/switching-graph framework, the semi-conservative requirement as preservation of symmetric lists, and the comparison between a weak near-unanimity polymorphism and a 3-NU (majority) polymorphism. It is already very close to the paper’s sharper introductory formulation. The main technical mismatch is that the 3-NU operation should be a polymorphism of the switching graph S_H, not of H itself. ([drops.dagstuhl.de](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2020/12688/pdf/LIPIcs-MFCS-2020-20.pdf))
missing_details: The operation should be stated on the switching graph: formally, a 3-NU here is a polymorphism phi: V(S_H)^3 -> V(S_H), not phi: H^3 -> H. ([drops.dagstuhl.de](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2020/12688/pdf/LIPIcs-MFCS-2020-20.pdf))

To be stand-alone, the question should define a br-graph in the paper’s sense, rather than assuming the reader already knows the term. The paper’s abstract makes clear that the intended scope is the class of signed graphs switchable to one in which every negative edge is also positive. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.07764))

The switching graph S_H should be defined explicitly: it has two copies of each vertex of H, and symmetric lists are those closed under swapping the two copies of each original vertex. ([drops.dagstuhl.de](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2020/12688/pdf/LIPIcs-MFCS-2020-20.pdf))

‘Semi-conservative’ should be stated precisely as preserving every symmetric unary relation/list, not just mentioned informally. ([drops.dagstuhl.de](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2020/12688/pdf/LIPIcs-MFCS-2020-20.pdf))
A weak near-unanimity polymorphism should be quantified as an operation of some arity k >= 3; the comparison object is specifically ternary. Your draft leaves the arity of the WNU implicit.

If you want the paper-faithful research framing, you should note that this equivalence is introduced as the refinement of Conjecture 1.1, and Theorem 1.3 proves the refined conjectural statement for reflexive br-graphs. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.07764))
refined_question: For a br-graph H in the sense of the paper, let S_H denote its switching graph, and call a polymorphism of S_H semi-conservative if it preserves every symmetric unary relation X subseteq V(S_H) (equivalently, every symmetric list, i.e. every X closed under swapping the two copies of each vertex of H in S_H). Is it true that S_H admits a semi-conservative weak near-unanimity polymorphism if and only if S_H admits a semi-conservative ternary near-unanimity polymorphism, that is, a polymorphism phi: V(S_H)^3 -> V(S_H) satisfying phi(x,x,y) = phi(x,y,x) = phi(y,x,x) = x for all x,y in V(S_H)? ([drops.dagstuhl.de](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2020/12688/pdf/LIPIcs-MFCS-2020-20.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Using Proposition 1.2 to sharpen Conjecture 1.1: for a br-graph H, is the list-switch homomorphism problem LSwHom(H) polynomial-time solvable if and only if its switching graph S_H admits a semi-conservative 3-NU polymorphism? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.07764))
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s introductory algebraic refinement rather than the broader surrounding discussion: the abstract explicitly says that the paper gives two characterisations, with the second refining the first, and proves the refined version for reflexive br-graphs. Your wording tracks that refinement, namely the replacement of the semi-conservative WNU condition by a semi-conservative 3-NU condition. The rewrite therefore keeps the problem narrow, restores the missing stand-alone definitions (especially the domain S_H and the meaning of semi-conservative/symmetric lists), and avoids broadening to the full complexity conjecture except in the optional equivalent formulation explicitly motivated by Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3. No ambient field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifier issues arise for this graph-polymorphism question. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.07764))
